title: Half-token experiment playbook
content:
Goal: explore a user-facing mode that reduces per-response token cost by ~40–60% with minimal UX regression. Not a new model — a serving/response shaping layer that prunes, compresses, or substitutes common phrases, plus optional compact summarization for long context.

Why: customers keep asking for ways to reduce token spend without losing perceived quality. We have caching + quantization gains, but many apps still use chat-style responses with lots of boilerplate. Quick win for Hosted tier and Dedicated cost recommendations.

Hypotheses:
- H1: For short assistant responses (<= 120 tokens), heuristic compression + phrase substitution can cut token count by ~45% and retain user satisfaction >= 85% of baseline.
- H2: For long-form answers (> 400 tokens), progressive condensation (inline micro-summaries + optional expanded view) keeps perceived helpfulness while dropping tokens by ~50%.

User stories (rough):
- As a product manager, I want an "economy" response mode so my app can reduce LLM bills for high-volume flows.
- As an end-user, I want concise answers by default but an easy way to expand into full detail.
- As an ops engineer, I want to measure cost savings and rollback if regressions spike.

Core ideas / sketches:
1) Compact templates + phrase map: replace common constructs ("Sure — here's a quick overview:") with 1–2 token markers that the client can expand locally. Server stores marker->expansion mapping.
2) Inline condensation: identify low-information clauses, collapse to bullets or parentheses. Use selective summarization of trailing context.
3) Progressive reveal: return summary + compressed body; include tokenized delta to allow client to request full body (costly).
4) Reified snippets: detect repeated boilerplate across responses and return a pointer to cached snippet. Customer can opt-in to snippet cache at route level.

API sketch (proto):
POST /v1/responses
body: { model, input, economy_mode: "compact"|"aggressive"|null, expand_token_placeholder: true }
response: { text_compressed: "...", expansion_map: {"#S0": "Here's a quick overview..."}, expand_endpoint: "/v1/responses/expand?ref=abc123" }
Notes: compression markers should be short (1–3 char safe tokens) and reserved in a model-agnostic way.

Metrics / success criteria:
- token delta: median tokens per response down 40–60% in target flows
- quality: human eval score >= 0.85 relative to baseline on a 5-point helpfulness scale
- conversion: no more than 3% rollback rate in first month for customers who opt-in
- latency: additional server-side processing < 12ms P50 after batching (target)

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Week 0–1: design compression heuristics (phrase map + simple clause splitter) and local expand SDK for web clients.
- Week 2: build prototype in sandbox hosted infra, implement expansion endpoint, basic snippet cache.
- Week 3: run A/B against control on small set of internal users / partner app. Collect token stats + NPS micro-survey.
- Week 4–6: iterate rules, add model-driven fallback (if compressed quality low, return full).

Success gating for wider rollout:
- token savings >40% on at least 3 app archetypes (support answers, search summaries, assistant hints)
- no major semantic regressions flagged in evals (QA review < 5% false/misleading truncations)
- engineering: expansion and cache stable at expected QPS with memory budget < 1GB per route

Operational considerations / risks:
- Safety: compressed output may accidentally drop safety-critical context. Need explicit rule: do not compress safety / compliance-related phrases (detect via classifiers).
- Traceability: need token-level telemetry and labeling so customers can see when compression was applied.
- Compatibility: some models may tokenize placeholders awkwardly. Must validate marker choice per-tokenizer or use opaque references in response metadata.
- Client UX: naive clients might render placeholders literally. Provide SDK helper and examples and default off for simple clients.

Dependencies:
- KV snippet cache (infra / serving-runtime) — SRE + serving-runtime team
- SDK changes (js + python) for local expansion and UX patterns — developer-experience
- Eval harness for quality checks — research/applied-ml

Open questions / quick notes:
- What should be the default per-route? per-customer opt-in? propose route-level default = off, but console suggestion = "economy hint" for high-volume routes.
- How to price? offer as "economy mode" with same per-token pricing but fewer tokens billed because of compression? (billing and legal need review).
- Should expansion costs be charged separately? probably yes; need billing design.
- Could we do model-side compression (train or finetune a compact generator)? longer runway but better quality — track as R&D.

Next steps (this doc owner):
- sync with Mika (SDK) and Evan (cost analytics) week of 2026-02-23
- prototype token markers and run tokenizer collision test across top 6 supported models
- create JIRA epic and link PRD stub (JIRA-9876)

Scratch todo list (low fidelity):
- [ ] build phrase map (~150 most common beginnings/closings)
- [ ] small client SDK expand helper (JS + example react component)
- [ ] implement expand endpoint with rate limits + auth
- [ ] add telemetry flagging compressed responses
- [ ] write micro-survey to measure perceived helpfulness

Loose notes: keep this light and experimental. We will likely iterate to more model-driven approaches, but a serving-side heuristic could be shipping-fast and useful. Keep the UX non-surprising: default closed summaries and easy expand.

---
Personal thoughts: prefer "compact" and "aggressive" label rather than "half-token" in UI. Save the technical name for internal. Also want to test whether snippet pointers can be cached on edge CDN to avoid extra round trip on expand.

End of scratch playbook.
